chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Wahb ibn Hafs from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
No group of people will gather in a gathering without mentioning Allah, Exalted and Majestic, and without mentioning us, except that gathering will be a regret upon them on the Day of Judgment.
Then he said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Our mention is from the mention of Allah, and the mention of our enemies is from the mention of Satan.'

key_terms.ذِكْرُنَا: Our mention (referring to the Imams/Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of mentioning the Imams in Islamic gatherings according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq) to establish that *dhikr al-A'imma* is not merely a devotional act but an integral component of *dhikr Allah*, thereby elevating the status of the Imams to a divine attribute. The hadith further contextualizes this by contrasting the remembrance of the Imams with that of their enemies, which is equated to the remembrance of Satan, highlighting the theological link between loyalty to the Ahl al-Bayt and spiritual orientation. This serves as a foundational proof in Shia jurisprudence for the obligation of *dhikr al-A'imma* in gatherings to ensure their validity and prevent regret on the Day of Judgment.
